root_causes.unverified-claim: Asserted a result, fact, or state (tests pass, file saved, command worked) without checking it.
root_causes.stale-knowledge: Relied on training-time knowledge for something that changes: versions, APIs, office holders, prices, laws.
root_causes.hallucinated-reference: Invented something that does not exist: a package, function, flag, file, citation, URL, or quote.
root_causes.instruction-misread: Misunderstood, ignored, or dropped part of what the user actually asked for.
root_causes.assumption-unchecked: Silently filled a gap with a guess when it should have looked it up or asked.
root_causes.scope-creep: Changed or produced things nobody asked for, beyond the requested task.
root_causes.destructive-action: Took an irreversible or destructive action without a safeguard, dry run, or confirmation.
root_causes.context-loss: Worked from partial information: truncated output, forgotten earlier turns, or a summary mistaken for the whole.
root_causes.tool-misuse: Used a tool wrongly: wrong tool, wrong arguments, misread its output, or ignored its error.
root_causes.environment-mismatch: Assumed the wrong OS, shell, version, path, timezone, locale, encoding, or permission.
root_causes.overconfidence: Stated something uncertain as certain, or failed to flag the limits of what it knew.
root_causes.sycophancy: Agreed with or deferred to the user against the evidence, or softened a needed correction away.
root_causes.security-lapse: Exposed a secret, trusted untrusted input, or followed instructions injected through content.
root_causes.arithmetic-logic: Made a calculation, counting, date, unit, or reasoning error.
root_causes.persistence-failure: Gave up too early, or looped on the same failing approach instead of changing strategy.
root_causes.other: None of the above fits; explain in what_happened and propose a new category.

domains.coding: Writing, editing, reviewing, or running code.
domains.research: Looking things up, citing sources, answering factual questions.
domains.tool-use: Driving tools, browsers, APIs, or other agents.

detected_by.user: The user noticed and pointed it out.
detected_by.self: The agent caught its own mistake.
detected_by.test: A test, linter, validator, or CI run caught it.
detected_by.tool-error: A tool returned an error that exposed it.
detected_by.reviewer: Another person or agent reviewing the work caught it.

statuses.seed: Written by maintainers to bootstrap the log from well-known failure patterns. Not yet independently confirmed.
statuses.reviewed: Submitted by the community and accepted by a human moderator.
statuses.confirmed: Reviewed, and independently reported or marked helpful by at least 3 separate reporters.
statuses.disputed: Conflicting feedback; returned only on request and with a warning.
statuses.deprecated: No longer applies (tools changed, or superseded). Kept for history, excluded from search.

severities.medium: Wrong output the user had to catch and correct.
severities.high: Lost work, a misleading result someone relied on, or real cost.
severities.critical: Data loss, a security incident, or harm outside the session.
